system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. The readout covered four weeks in the standard SMB segment and the usual reporting cadence.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

memory_block.body: Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.
Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. The readout covered four weeks in the standard SMB segment and the usual reporting cadence.
Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.
Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

answer.rationale:
The current situation has two internal, structural symptoms (activation -6% QoQ, onboarding completion -4% QoQ) and one external shock (competitor entry pricing). The competitor is the loudest signal, but promotional pricing is the direction whose inherited evidence is weakest relative to the objective: memory_73 reads as a four-week readout on the standard SMB segment at the usual reporting cadence, i.e. a window that can measure acquisition and gross revenue lift but cannot see discount-cohort retention, margin, or whether the acquired revenue is qualified. Matching a price attack on that basis risks buying exactly the low-value, high-churn cohort the competitor is fishing for, and permanently repricing the SMB segment. So I am spending a verification pull on memory_73 specifically to see whether the original record measured any post-promotion retention or margin at all, or only the four-week acquisition lift.

My intended action addresses both internal declines at once: onboarding simplification is supported by two independent inherited records (memory_31 on signup field reduction, memory_86 on shortened onboarding) and is complementary to memory_91's activation messaging, which shares the same funnel stage. I am pulling memory_86 as the second verification because it is the memory I am actually acting on and its scope is stated as 'self-serve accounts' — I want the original record to confirm the lift was measured on the population currently declining, and to check whether the reported gains were completion-rate gains or actually carried through to revenue.

Downstream value risk is real even for my chosen direction and I am not treating the inherited claims as settled: cutting required fields at signup can raise activation while degrading lead qualification and sales routing, so a completion-rate win can silently reduce qualified revenue. memory_31's 'durable lift in first-week activation' is a first-week metric, not a revenue metric, and memory_44 indicates the higher-value enterprise path depends on sales-assisted qualification that signup data feeds. I will therefore run this as a standard experiment with guardrails on downstream qualified-pipeline quality and retention, not just completion, and I will keep field reduction to non-qualifying fields. If verification shows memory_86's lift was completion-only with no revenue follow-through, I will downscale to a guarded test rather than proceed at full scale. Enterprise sales assist and referral incentives are set aside not because they are disproven but because neither targets the declining self-serve funnel this week; referral incentives in particular (memory_57) were established on retained customers and would amplify, not repair, a weakening activation base.
